terminology_locked_this_session.importance: CRITICAL — this vocabulary must be used consistently in code comments, thesis prose, admin UI helper text, and all future documentation. The prior handoff did NOT lock these terms; they were debated and resolved in this session.

visit.definition: One entry in the queue management dashboard, represented by one appointments document in Firestore. Each day of clinical activity for a patient produces one visit.
visit.technical_anchor: One appointments doc, one caseDay, one clinicalPulse array, one forensicSeal

case.definition: The complete clinical encounter a patient experiences, consisting of one or more visits linked via originApptId pointers and tracked via caseDay counter. A same-day case is one case with one visit. A multi-day case (hospitalization) is one case with multiple visits, one per day of active care.
case.technical_anchor: Chain of appointments docs walked backward via useAncestorChain resolver

medical_record.definition: A signed SOAP document in the medical_records Firestore collection, created when a clinician signs off on their clinical notes during a visit. Immutable once signed. Each visit may produce zero, one, or more medical records depending on how many discrete consultations occur.
medical_record.technical_anchor: Docs in medical_records collection with legal.isLocked: true
medical_record.note: The Firestore collection name stays 'medical_records' — no rename needed, matches this term exactly

appointment.definition: Pet-owner-facing terminology for a visit. The mobile app says 'appointment'; the admin dashboard says 'visit'. Deliberate audience-specific naming.
appointment.used_in: mobile client app (VetConnect/), pet owner communications

continuation_via_confine.definition: A form of case continuation where the patient physically stays in the clinic overnight. Old visit reaches terminal carried-over status; new visit is created for next day with originApptId backward pointer, caseDay incremented, and starting status 'confined'.
continuation_via_confine.trigger: EndOfDayModal Active silo CONFINE button (action value: 'hospitalize')
continuation_via_confine.clinical_meaning: Pet is hospitalized, clinic retains overnight care responsibility

continuation_via_carry_over_rebook.definition: A form of case continuation where the patient goes home overnight. Old visit reaches terminal carried-over status; new visit is created for next day with originApptId backward pointer, caseDay incremented, and starting status 'confirmed' (pre-arrival scheduled state).
continuation_via_carry_over_rebook.trigger: EndOfDayModal Active silo Carry-Over button (action value: 'rebook')
continuation_via_carry_over_rebook.clinical_meaning: Pet went home for the night because visit was unfinished but not clinically requiring overnight stay. Re-arrives next day as a scheduled visit.
continuation_via_carry_over_rebook.naming_note: THE BUTTON LABELED 'Carry-Over' CORRESPONDS TO ACTION VALUE 'rebook'. This is the user's explicit correction of a prior framing mistake — CONFINE and Carry-Over are siblings, not CONFINE vs carry-over.

follow_up.definition: A separate operation triggered at sign-off when the clinician schedules a future recheck visit. Unlike continuation, a follow-up begins a NEW case (caseDay resets to 1) and uses DIFFERENT linkage fields (parentAppointmentId + parentRecordId) to soft-reference the prior case for clinical context.
follow_up.trigger: ClinicalWorkspace.handleSaveConsult when soapData.nextVisit is set (currently non-functional because nextVisit UI missing — see T2.28-expanded)
follow_up.clinical_meaning: Prior visit is clinically complete; this is a recheck or continuation encounter happening later after pet has been home
follow_up.why_different_from_continuation: See architecture_insights.dual_linkage_rationale — forcing follow-ups through originApptId would corrupt forensic metrics, ghost gating, caseDay counter, and EndOfDayModal day navigation

dual_linkage_rationale.summary: VetConnect has TWO linkage mechanisms for cross-visit relationships: originApptId (for continuation = same case across days) and parentAppointmentId+parentRecordId (for follow-up = new case referencing prior). They are NOT interchangeable.
why_not_unified: useAncestorChain walks via originApptId and treats the chain as ONE continuous temporal thread for forensic math. Follow-ups with 7-day gaps would corrupt recordAge, opHoursAge, and total metrics.
calculatePulseMetrics aggregates duration across the chain — correct for hospitalization (one continuous case) but meaningless for follow-ups (unrelated encounters separated by home time).
EndOfDayModal day navigation uses uniqueDates from combined pulse — follow-ups would create 7-day gaps between 'Day 1' and 'Day 2' arrows.
caseDay counter implicitly maps to calendar days for continuous care — follow-ups would report 'Day 8 of case started 7 days ago' which is semantically false.
Ghost gating midnight-caps abandoned segments — designed for single-day gaps, not multi-day follow-up windows.
dual_linkage_rationale.implication: Trying to force follow-ups through originApptId would require 5+ special-case workarounds in downstream consumers. Two linkage fields is cheaper AND more honest about the semantic difference.

audit_system_mechanics.pulse_event_structure: Each appointment doc has a clinicalPulse: [] array appended via arrayUnion. Each event: {eventId, type, fromStatus, toStatus, timestamp, staffId, staffName, note, [correctedEventId]}
audit_system_mechanics.correction_dna_link_pattern: Reverts create a CORRECTION event with correctedEventId pointing at the invalidated event. Calculator builds voidedIds Set to skip voided segments from math while preserving them in display. Sophisticated structured soft-delete.
audit_system_mechanics.dual_clock_routing: Business-hour clock for queue/consult states (respects openHour/closeHour/workingDays); absolute wall-clock for confined states (hospitalization is 24/7). Routed via CONFINED_STATES.has(status) ? 'absolute' : 'business' at pulseUtils.js:150.
audit_system_mechanics.midnight_gating: isGhostSegment at pulseUtils.js:147 caps abandoned queue/consult segments at day-end to prevent stale records from accumulating fake duration. Does NOT apply to confined (correctly).
audit_system_mechanics.forensic_seal_semantics: forensicSeal is a SNAPSHOT, not a LOCK. Written by markNoShow, rejectAppointment, deferAppointment, rescheduleAppointment, triage wizard paths. NOT currently written on normal sign-off completion (T2.44 closes this gap). NOT cleared on revertStatus (T2.42 fixes this drift).
audit_system_mechanics.discharge_anchor: pulseUtils.js:93-101 — if the LAST event in combined history is terminal, freeze the clock at that moment. Otherwise use current time.
